To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stochastic fluctuations in gene expression can be characterized by single-molecule analysis of transcription factor expression in single bacteria, and that stochastic fluctuations in transcription factor expression are minimized by autoregulation.
(i) stochasticity in gene regulation is determined by the expression level and (ii) extrinsic noise and negative autoregression minimize transcription factor concentration heterogeneity.

stochastic expression dynamics of a fate-determinating transcription factor, cI, is determined by its expression level and is largely extrinsic, and that autoregulatory circuit minimizes cell-to-cell variation in cI expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of gene expression, and how cells control stochastic expression of transcription factors that regulate their own expression.
understanding how stochastic gene expression contributes to cell-fate determination, and how cells control stochastic gene expression to achieve precise gene regulation.
understanding stochasticity in transcription factor expression and how cells regulate this stochasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intrinsic noise is not affected by the autoregulation of the transcription factor cI, but that extrinsic noise is reduced by autoregulation.

the stochasticity in gene regulatory networks is determined by the intrinsic stochasticity of the transcription factor, the extrinsic noise of the transcription factor and the intrinsic stochasticity and extrinsic noise of other components in the regulatory network.
the expression of the CI transcription factor is subject to both intrinsic and extrinsic noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we quantitatively studied the stochastic expression of a fate-determinating transcription factor, cI, in a bacteriophage λ-infected cell.

stochastic expression dynamics of a key transcription factor is determined by a combination of intrinsic and extrinsic noise, and autoregulation can counteract extrinsic noise and introduce memory to minimize the stochasticity.
stochasticity in gene regulation is a major determinant of cell-to-cell heterogeneity and that cells use negative feedback to minimize stochastic fluctuations in gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

stochasticity in gene regulatory networks, such as those that regulate fate determination, is largely determined by extrinsic noise, which arises from the cell-to-cell variability in the expression of the regulatory genes and their targets.
the intrinsic and extrinsic sources of noise are not independent, but are coupled.
the stochasticity of gene expression is not determined solely by the intrinsic properties of a gene, but rather is influenced by a combination of extrinsic noise and intrinsic noise.
